newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bank PBK seeks stake in Warta.
newsitem.headline: Polish bank PBK seeks stake in Warta.

text.p: Poland's Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK), slated for sale by the end of April this year, is interested in becoming a significant investor in insurer Warta, PBK's president said on Thursday.

"We would like to be a significant investor in Warta. We don't want one or two percent. We want at least five percent of the company," Andrzej Podsiadlo told reporters after a news conference on Thursday.
Warta, Poland's second largest insurance company, plans in February to issue between 865,380 and 2,596,139 shares to Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH), Kredyt Bank, PBK and two current shareholders.
Currently Warta has 3.46 million shares outstanding and its main stockholders are the state treasury, with a 34.7 percent stake, and Elektrim with 10.1 percent.
Podsiadlo also said PBK was not currently interested in buying more stock in Polish Development Bank (PBR), or Kredyt Bank, which, together with PBK and Warta, want to create a financial group.
"PBK at the moment does not plan to buy shares from the new PBR issue...nor any of BPH's convertible bonds, or any shares of Kredyt Bank," Podsiadlo said.
On Wednesday PBR said its planned 8.4-million-share issue was designed to attract strategic investors and help finance its participation in the planned banking-insurance group.
Kredyt Bank is offering large investors eight million shares next month.
PBK currently holds 33 percent of PBR shares and 21.5 percent of Kredyt Bank.

On Wednesday PBR said it was interested in buying up to 15 percent of PBK in its privatisation and both Kredyt Bank and BPH have signalled their interest in the privatisation, without saying how large a stake they would seek.
The finance ministry plans by the end of April to sell 65 percent of PBK to a foreign or domestic strategic investor and follow it with a public offering of 15 percent around October.
